pageCache.pageTitle: Home - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Strive to succeed in the presence of God
Welcome to St Monica’s School
Welcome to St Monica’s School
I am very proud to be the Headteacher of this wonderful school. I have worked at St Monica’s for twenty-five years and have had the privilege of serving as Headteacher for twenty of them. We are fortunate to have a highly experienced, dedicated and stable staff team and for many of us, St Monica’s truly feels like a second home.
St Monica’s is a thriving two-form entry Catholic primary school situated in the heart of our local community near Southgate. Our Catholic faith is at the centre of everything we do and shapes the caring, inclusive and nurturing environment that makes our school such a special place to learn and grow. Guided by Gospel values, we encourage every child to recognise their unique God-given gifts and talents and to use them in the service of others.
One of the highlights of my day is welcoming children at the school gate each morning and seeing them run happily into the playground. Our pupils are confident, enthusiastic learners who take pride in their achievements and demonstrate high standards of behaviour, respect and kindness towards one another. We have high expectations for every child and are committed to ensuring that all pupils achieve their very best academically.
Alongside academic excellence, we place equal importance on the development of the whole child: intellectually, spiritually, socially, emotionally and creatively. We work closely with parents, carers and our parish community to help children develop a strong sense of faith, compassion and responsibility, preparing them to make a positive contribution to the wider world.
As a parent of three children myself, I have always led the school with one simple principle in mind: “Would this be good enough for my child?” This question continues to guide our decisions and our commitment to providing the very best education and care for every pupil entrusted to us.
Please explore our website to find out more about life at St Monica’s and visit our Admissions page if you are interested in applying for a place. We look forward to welcoming you to our school community.
Get in touch
Headteacher Mrs Kate Baptiste
AddressCannon Road, Southgate London, N14 7HE

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching (CST) is the Church’s guidance on how we live our faith by caring for others and God’s world. It teaches us to love our neighbour, to stand up for fairness and dignity, and to look after the most vulnerable. At our school, Catholic Social Teaching helps children understand that their choices and actions matter, encouraging them to be kind, respectful, and responsible members of school family and the wider community.
At the beginning of each half term, we explore a pillar of CST. We start with an introductory Collective Worship and this is followed up with a lesson in class.
We support a range of charities including Macmillan Cancer, our St Monica’s Catholic School Foodbank and other charities that are brought to our attention, for example the orphanage in the Democratic Republic of Congo, CAFOD and NSPCC.
Catholic Social Teaching Intent Statement
Catholic Social Teaching Overview
Chaplaincy Team working at the Christmas Bazaar!
World Book Day – when the whole community comes together!
Every year, during Lent, the whole school makes a pilgrimage to the food bank at St Monica’s Church. The children gift whatever they can afford in the way of food for our local community who rely so much on this invaluable resource. It is a powerful witness to God’s love.
At our annual Harvest Festival, children bring cash donations which the volunteers use to buy food. Their foodbank is available to everyone every Monday morning.
At our annual Summer Fete and Christmas Bazaar, the strength of our school and parish community is evident in the way that parents, children, staff and parishioners come together to celebrate, support one another and raise valuable funds for the school. These events reflect the principles of Catholic Social Teaching, particularly the call to Community and Participation and Care for God’s Creation. Our Friends’ Association actively promotes local businesses, helping to strengthen community links and support the local economy. We also encourage sustainable practices through initiatives such as the sale of pre-loved school uniform, helping to reduce waste and protect our environment. In previous years, event themes have focused on caring for our common home, inspiring children and families to reflect on their responsibility to love and protect God’s creation. With performances from our school choir and a wide range of activities for all ages, these events are a joyful celebration of faith, fellowship and service.
Our annual visits to Parliament with the School Council are organised by Mrs Weston. They provide an excellent opportunity for pupils to see the principles of Catholic Social Teaching in action. Children learn about democracy, participation and the common good, developing an understanding of how individuals can work together to create a fairer society and serve their local and wider communities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prayer & Liturgy - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Prayer & Liturgy
Prayer & Liturgy
Prayer and liturgy are at the heart of the Catholic life of our school. Children pray throughout the day, including at the beginning and end of each school day and before and after meals. Daily collective worship provides opportunities for pupils to grow in faith through prayer, reflection and scripture, whether in whole-school celebrations, phase groups or individual classes. Our worship is led by staff, pupils and members of the parish team, and includes both traditional prayers and opportunities for spontaneous prayer. We are blessed to have strong links with St Monica’s Parish; our priests are regular visitors and we celebrate Mass in school at least once every half term, as well as on Holy Days of Obligation. Throughout the year, our children deepen their relationship with God through Masses, retreat days, the May Procession and other special liturgical celebrations, helping them to live out our Catholic faith in their daily lives.

We have a strong devotion to Our Lady and during May have a special Marion procession which all families are also invited to.
The heavy rain on the Feast of Corpus Christi meant that our usual procession and Benediction had to happen inside school. Year 6 led the procession and our altar servers as ever did a fantastic job supporting Fr Sean as he held the Blessed Sacrament in the monstrance.
Our worship also takes place at St Monica’s Catholic Church where we always hold our Junior Carol Services. Here is one from Years 5 and 6.
Our annual Infant Passion Services (led by the children) lead Year 2 parents through the events of Holy Week in a prayerful and reflective way, helping us all to prepare for Holy Week.
We are fortunate to have a music specialist on the staff, Mr Charles-Nelson who enhances all our worship with rousing and powerful singing.
Every year we reflect on Holy Week through a special Passion Service. We are joined by Year 4 parents for the Junior one. It is a thought provoking and reflective occasion starting with Palm Sunday and finishing with Jesus’ death on the cross.
We have been fortunate to have a few visits from Bishop John Sherrington, before his move to Liverpool. Sometimes he has led a Mass and others a special assembly. He came in 2024 to celebrate the 70th anniversary of St Monica’s Catholic School!
We were delighted to welcome Bishop John Sherrington to school for a special visit. After leading a Collective Worship, Bishop John visited all classrooms and answered questions about his role and responsibilities as a Bishop.
Children are confident to spontaneously lead prayer services in response to events, such as our school fish dying.
During October, month of the Holy Rosary and May, month of Our Lady, we pray a decade of the Rosary every morning before school. We have a rota so that each class can take a turn in leading it and parents and carers are invited to join us for this special devotion.

RHE
RHE
Relationships and Health Education (RHE) in Catholic primary schools within the Diocese of Westminster is taught in partnership with parents and rooted firmly in the teachings of the Catholic Church. It helps children to understand how to build loving, respectful relationships, to value themselves and others as made in the image of God, and to develop healthy attitudes to their bodies and emotions. RHE is delivered in an age-appropriate way, promoting virtues such as respect, kindness, responsibility and self-care, while supporting children to grow spiritually, morally and emotionally.

pageCache.pageTitle: Racial Justice Equality and Diversity - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Racial Justice Equality and Diversity
“By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” (John 13:35)
This verse from the Gospel of John lies at the heart of the Diocese of Westminster’s commitment to Racial Justice, Equality and Diversity (RJED). The call to love our neighbour extends to all people, regardless of race, ethnicity, culture or background, recognising the God-given dignity and worth of every individual. As a Catholic community, we strive to build a society rooted in equality, inclusion and mutual respect, where diversity is celebrated and everyone is able to flourish.
At St Monica’s Catholic Primary School, RJED is an integral part of our Catholic life and mission. Rooted in the belief that every person is created in the image and likeness of God, we help our children to recognise, value and respect the rich diversity of our local, national and global communities. Through our curriculum, collective worship, prayer and daily interactions, we promote justice, challenge prejudice and discrimination, and foster a culture of belonging where everyone is welcomed, respected and treated with dignity.
Throughout the year, pupils engage in a range of activities that celebrate diversity and promote anti-racism. A particular highlight is our participation in Show Racism the Red Card each October, when the whole school wears red and takes part in learning activities that develop understanding of racism and the importance of being actively anti-racist. Our annual International Day in May provides another opportunity to celebrate the many cultures, languages and traditions represented within our school community.
We are also proud that Mrs Baptiste represents the school as a member of the Diocese of Westminster’s RJED committee. Through this collaborative work, schools across the Diocese contribute to the development of curriculum resources, policies and best practice, helping to ensure that racial justice, equality and diversity remain central to Catholic education.
Prayer from KS1 from Westminster Diocesan Schools
Prayers from KS2 from Westminster Diocesan Schools
Every year in May, to link with International Day, we invite children to wear national dress or flag colours. Our hall is decorated with flags and parents are invited to set up a stall to reflect their heritage. Countries represented are from all seven continents! Children enjoy tasting food, learning languages and experiencing some of the culture from other countries. We are always grateful to the parents for giving their time so freely. Check out the newsletter every May (around 21st) to see the photos from other celebratory days.
Our children led a powerful and moving dance at the Enfield Schools’ Dance Festival, in response to Martin Luther’s speech, ‘I have a dream’. “Imagine a world where people would not be judged by the colour of their skin, but by the content of their character.”

pageCache.text:
Saints
Saints
Although the current school building opened in 1954, the origins of St Monica’s Catholic Primary School can be traced back to the early 1900s when it began as a small hut beside the church. Through the collective efforts of the parish priest and parishioners, funds were raised to purchase a plot of land approximately one mile from the church. This is where the school remains today.
As our namesake, Saint Monica holds a special place in our school community. Children learn about her as the Patron Saint of Mothers and how, through her faithful and persistent prayers for her son Augustine, he eventually converted to Christianity and later became Saint Augustine, one of the most influential saints of the Church.

pageCache.pageTitle: Westminster Diocese - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Westminster Diocese
Westminster Diocese
St Monica’s Catholic Primary School works with Westminster Diocese to ensure that the school operates in accordance with the teachings and values of the Catholic Church. This includes ensuring that the curriculum aligns with Catholic teachings, that religious education is integrated into the school’s programmes and that the school maintains a Catholic identity.
Westminster Diocese provides support and resources to the school. This includes financial assistance, professional development opportunities for teachers, access to educational materials and resources and guidance on matters related to Catholic education.
Additionally, working with Westminster Diocese allows the school to be part of a larger Catholic educational community. This provides opportunities for collaboration, sharing best practices and networking with other Catholic schools in the area. This also allows the school to participate in Diocesan events, initiatives and programs promoting Catholic education and fostering unity among Catholic schools.
Westminster Diocese plays a role in ensuring the school’s adherence to Catholic teachings and values. They guide faith formation, sacramental preparation and religious practices within the school community.
Working with The Diocese, helps ensure that St Monica’s maintains its Catholic identity and mission.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast & After School Club - St Monica's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Club
For all enquiries about Breakfast Club or After School Club, please email Mrs Murphy (breakfast) and Mrs Weston (after school) on breakfast.afterschoolclub@st-monicas.enfield.sch.uk. Alternatively telephone the school office on 0208 886 4647 between 8:30am and 4pm.
If you are a current family using the service and need to change or add days, you must give 24 hours’ notice. The latest time to contact Mrs Murphy or Mrs Weston about booking an ad hoc session for the following day is 4:30pm.
Our Breakfast and After School Clubs are run by school staff on the school site.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast club starts at 7:30am with breakfast of cereal (porridge, Weetabix, Cornflakes or Rice Krispies), toast, a range of fruit and a drink (water or milk). Children will eat on arrival to the club. It is £5.50 for the session.
After School Club
After School Club runs until 6pm. A snack is served at 3.15pm. Allergies and/or intolerances must be recorded on the CONTACT FORM. If you would like your child to eat a meal in the afternoon, you can send them in with a packed tea (please provide this in a lunch box with a cool pack enclosed). Please ensure that this is a healthy meal with no sweets or fizzy drinks. We recommend things like: pasta/couscous salad, wraps, bagels, sandwiches, chopped fruit and/or vegetables. No family size packs of crisps and absolutely no nuts (which includes pesto) or hummus (containing sesame). Children can fill up their water bottle in school – no need to provide additional drinks.
Apply for a Place
To apply for a place for Breakfast and/or After School Club, please read the Terms and Conditions carefully and completing the Application Form found below.
Breakfast & ASC application form
Prior to your child starting, you must complete the Contact Form below.
Information about healthy meals
Requests for payment are payable in advance each month. Any parents who are using tax free child care, child care vouchers or a salary sacrifice scheme, please contact Catherine Nolan on finance@st-monicas.enfield.sch.uk to register this. Many thanks.

pageCache.text:
Religious Education at St Monica’s
Religious Education across the school is structured around the six branches set out in the Religious Education Directory (RED), a programme of study approved by the Bishops’ Conference. The aims of the RED are used to inform learning objectives. Teaching and learning is organised around the four key areas of the RED: Revelation, Church, Celebration and Life in Christ. Lessons place a strong emphasis on making meaningful connections between Scripture, the traditions of the Church and pupils’ own lived experiences, with regular opportunities for reflection. In addition, the sixth branch focuses on the study of World Faiths, with different year groups exploring Judaism and Islam in greater depth. 10% of the weekly taught curriculum is allocated to Religious Education. We work closely with St Monica’s Parish and strive to make links with other religious traditions. Home, school and parish work together as no one group can easily succeed alone.
